5.8 Syntax Rules for GROUP BY Queries under sql_mode=only_full_group_by

-- MySQL:
   Method:
      Core Constraint: The only_full_group_by mode enforces that GROUP BY queries must follow the rule: "Columns in the SELECT list must be either grouping columns in the GROUP BY clause, or wrapped by aggregate functions (MAX/MIN/SUM/ANY_VALUE, etc.)". If there is no GROUP BY clause (aggregate query without GROUP BY), the SELECT list cannot contain non-aggregated columns;
      Error Scenario: Violating the constraint throws error 1140 ("Mixing of GROUP columns with no GROUP columns is illegal if there is no GROUP BY clause") or error 1055 ("Expression #N of SELECT list is not in GROUP BY clause and contains nonaggregated column ... which is not functionally dependent on columns in GROUP BY clause");
      Solutions: ① Add the non-aggregated column to the GROUP BY clause; ② Wrap the non-aggregated column with an aggregate function (e.g., ANY_VALUE(non_aggregated_column)); ③ Temporarily disable only_full_group_by (SET sql_mode=(SELECT REPLACE(@@sql_mode,'ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY','')), not recommended for production).
   eg:
      Example violating the rule (corresponding to problem scenario 1404):
      SELECT id, COUNT(*) FROM users; (No GROUP BY but SELECT contains non-aggregated column id, triggers error 1140)
      Solution 1: Add GROUP BY column
      SELECT id, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY id;
      Solution 2: Wrap non-aggregated column with ANY_VALUE
      SELECT ANY_VALUE(id), COUNT(*) FROM users;
      Correct example of GROUP BY query:
      SELECT department, MAX(salary), ANY_VALUE(location) FROM employees GROUP BY department; (location is not a GROUP BY column, wrapped with ANY_VALUE)

question: As of the present, what is the full name of the youngest racer? Indicate her nationality and the name of the race to which he/she first joined.
nl2_rewrite: --- Source & Joins - Source table: 'drivers' - Link 'drivers' to 'driverstandings' using 'drivers.driverId' = 'driverstandings.driverId' - Link 'driverstandings' to 'races' using 'driverstandings.raceId' = 'races.raceId' --- Filters - Identify the youngest driver by selecting the record(s) in 'drivers' where 'dob' = the maximum value of 'drivers.dob' across all drivers --- Aggregation & Computation - For the youngest driver, find all related records in 'driverstandings' - For those records, determine the earliest race they joined by selecting the minimum value of 'races.date' - If multiple races share this same earliest date for that driver, select the one(s) with that minimum 'races.date' - Create a derived column 'full_name' = concatenation of 'drivers.forename' and 'drivers.surname' --- Ordering & Limit - When identifying the youngest driver, order drivers by 'dob' in descending order and select the top 1 (or equivalently use MAX(dob)) - When identifying the first race for that driver, order the joined races by 'races.date' in ascending order and select the top 1 --- Return - full_name (drivers.forename + drivers.surname) - drivers.nationality - races.name
first_generated_sql: SELECT      CONCAT(d.forename, ' ', d.surname) AS full_name,     d.nationality,     r.name AS race_name FROM drivers d JOIN driverstandings ds ON d.driverId = ds.driverId JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId WHERE d.dob = (SELECT MAX(dob) FROM drivers) ORDER BY r.date ASC LIMIT 1;
second_generated_sql: SELECT      CONCAT(d.forename, ' ', d.surname) AS full_name,     d.nationality,     r.name AS race_name FROM (     SELECT driverId, forename, surname, nationality     FROM drivers     ORDER BY dob DESC     LIMIT 1 ) d JOIN driverstandings ds ON d.driverId = ds.driverId JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId ORDER BY r.date ASC LIMIT 1;

question: For the client whose loan was approved first in 1993/7/5, what is the increase rate of his/her account balance from 1993/3/22 to 1998/12/27?
nl2_rewrite: --- Source & Joins - Source tables: 'loan', 'account', 'trans' - Link 'loan' and 'account' using 'loan.account_id' = 'account.account_id' - Link 'account' and 'trans' using 'account.account_id' = 'trans.account_id' --- Filters - For identifying the client: filter 'loan.date' = 1993-07-05 - Among loans on 1993-07-05, identify the loan with the earliest approval time on that date (if only date is stored and no time exists, treat all loans on that date as tied and select the one with the minimum 'loan.loan_id' as a deterministic tie-breaker) - After selecting that single 'loan.account_id', filter 'trans.account_id' to this account only - For balance on Date B: filter 'trans.date' = 1993-03-22 - For balance on Date A: filter 'trans.date' = 1998-12-27 --- Aggregation & Computation - For the selected account, determine 'balance_B' as the 'trans.balance' on 1993-03-22 (if multiple transactions exist on that date, use the record with the latest transaction time on that date; if time is not available, use the record with the maximum 'trans_id' on that date) - For the selected account, determine 'balance_A' as the 'trans.balance' on 1998-12-27 (same rule: if multiple records, use the one with the latest transaction on that date, or maximum 'trans_id' if no time) - Calculate 'increase_rate' = ((balance_A - balance_B) / balance_B) * 100 --- Return - increase_rate
first_generated_sql: SELECT      ((balance_A - balance_B) * 1.0 / NULLIF(balance_B, 0)) * 100 AS increase_rate FROM (     SELECT          MAX(CASE WHEN t.date = '1998-12-27' THEN t.balance END) AS balance_A,         MAX(CASE WHEN t.date = '1993-03-22' THEN t.balance END) AS balance_B     FROM (         SELECT              t1.account_id         FROM loan l         JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id         WHERE l.date = '1993-07-05'         ORDER BY l.loan_id         LIMIT 1     ) target_account     JOIN trans t ON target_account.account_id = t.account_id     WHERE t.date IN ('1993-03-22', '1998-12-27')     GROUP BY t.account_id     HAVING          MAX(CASE WHEN t.date = '1993-03-22' THEN t.trans_id END) IS NOT NULL          AND MAX(CASE WHEN t.date = '1998-12-27' THEN t.trans_id END) IS NOT NULL ) balances;
second_generated_sql: SELECT ((balance_A - balance_B) * 1.0 / NULLIF(balance_B, 0)) * 100 AS increase_rate FROM (     SELECT          (SELECT t1.balance           FROM trans t1           WHERE t1.account_id = target_account.account_id             AND t1.date = '1998-12-27'           ORDER BY t1.trans_id DESC           LIMIT 1) AS balance_A,         (SELECT t2.balance           FROM trans t2           WHERE t2.account_id = target_account.account_id             AND t2.date = '1993-03-22'           ORDER BY t2.trans_id DESC           LIMIT 1) AS balance_B     FROM (         SELECT l.account_id         FROM loan l         JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id         WHERE l.date = '1993-07-05'         ORDER BY l.loan_id         LIMIT 1     ) AS target_account ) AS balances WHERE balance_B IS NOT NULL AND balance_A IS NOT NULL;
